notes: Translated from OVAL's default-semantics cases, which pose a request with no Asset, and the matching prohibition1-3 cases, which pose the same request with it. OVAL decides the target-less request by an evaluator switch (semantics_by_default: prohibit, permit, or unspecified by default). due2 has no default semantics: a request without a target makes every relation part U (workflows §3.2, §5.2, decided 2026-10-11, issue #26), so the verdict is Indeterminate whenever the target could decide it, and the default is the enforcement point's. OVAL's three answers to scenario 1 are the three completions a caller might choose; due2 reports that the request is underspecified. OVAL requests carry no time; request.at and effective_at are an arbitrary fixed instant.

scenarios.name: no target (default_sem4-6)

expected.why: The request names no target, so ex:policy:1010#prohibition's relation part is U: completing it T gives Deny, F gives NotApplicable. Indeterminate.

scenarios.oval_expected: reject (False) under semantics_by_default=-1; accept (True) under 1; not processed (None) under 0

expected.why: Action and target match; ex:policy:1010#prohibition applies and nothing overrides it.
